candidates.title: Fix /homepage desktop LCP regression (13-14s → <1.8s target)
candidates.why: Two consecutive prod traces show / desktop LCP at 13,060ms and 14,528ms — was 1,404ms in the S160 clean trace. The regression arrived with commit b5c422d1b333 (ambient bundle grew 114.9→130.0KB with nav-sheet.js + account-chip.js + S160 shell-hash rotation). FCP is also blown (11s+) which points to a render-blocking symptom or extreme TTFB. The bisect plan is proven: isolate by reverting nav-sheet.js from the ambient bundle first; if still blown, suspect account-chip.js making a synchronous Supabase call at bundle parse time; if still blown, check if the 114KB HTML + new shell hash caused a CDN edge miss cascade.
candidates.recipe: Run: node scripts/measure-page-performance.mjs --check --base=https://vaultsparkstudios.com to get current baseline. Then: temporarily remove nav-sheet.js from AMBIENT_SOURCES in build-ambient-bundle.mjs, rebuild, deploy to staging, re-trace. If LCP recovers, audit nav-sheet.js for synchronous blocking calls. Check account-chip.js for Supabase calls outside DOMContentLoaded. Check if index.html shell hash changed and CDN is serving stale intermediate.

candidates.title: Service-worker warm handoff on shell hash rotation (prevent cold-cache LCP spikes)
candidates.why: Every time `build-shell-assets.mjs` rotates a shell hash, every visitor cold-fetches the new bundle — the exact failure mode that produced the S161 LCP spike. The service worker already exists (VAPID + push); extending it to prefetch the incoming shell hash the moment the SW receives a push or the page emits a hash-change event would eliminate the cold-cache window entirely. No other studio site does this. It turns a recurring regression class into a non-event.
candidates.recipe: In scripts/build-shell-assets.mjs, write the outgoing hash → .cache/shell-manifest-prev.json before rotating. In the service worker (registered via pwa-nav.js), add a 'shell-prefetch' message handler that fetches /assets/ambient.shell-{newHash}.js into the cache. On shell rebuild, emit a BroadcastChannel('vs-shell-update') message with the new hash; SW listener prefetches it before any page navigates to it.

executionLog.note: S162: SW controls site-wide caching; warm-handoff is additive but unvalidatable without a real browser this session. Deferred per fragility memory.

candidates.title: Split 130KB ambient bundle: critical-path (<12KB) + enhancement layer (loaded post-DCL)
candidates.why: The ambient bundle has grown to 130KB across 23 sources — all loaded `defer` but still parsed synchronously after HTML. Sources like `nav-sheet.js`, `adaptive-speculation.js`, `gamification-layer.js`, and `vault-atlas.js` are enhancement-tier: they add progressive behavior but are not required for first-user comprehension. Splitting into a ≤12KB critical shell (theme toggle + nav open/close + cookie consent + CSP) vs a dynamically-injected enhancement bundle cuts the post-DCL parse budget by ~85% for new visitors, directly reducing Time to Interactive on cold cache.
candidates.recipe: In scripts/build-ambient-bundle.mjs, add a CRITICAL_SOURCES constant (≤6 files). Build two outputs: ambient.shell-{hash}.js (critical only) and ambient.enhance-{hash}.js (everything else). In build-shell-assets.mjs, inject the enhancement bundle via a tiny inline loader that appends it after DOMContentLoaded fires. Gate enhancement loading on Navigator.connection.saveData === false and deviceMemory ≥ 1.

executionLog.note: S162: re-scoped — bundle is already deferred (cannot block FCP); will not move headline; high re-regression risk. Shipped kit-fallback.js defer as a safe adjacent micro-win.

candidates.title: Activate RUM R2 bucket (code is production-ready from S154, blocked on binding)
candidates.why: Real-user monitoring code (`assets/rum-beacon.js` + Worker `/v/rum` endpoint + `scripts/rollup-rum.mjs`) has been production-ready since S154. The only blocker was `vaultspark-rum` R2 bucket creation — the Worker binding just needs wiring. Without RUM, every perf regression is diagnosed post-hoc via synthetic traces; with RUM active, the S161 LCP spike would have been caught within minutes of the push landing. This is the highest-leverage observability gap in the entire stack.
candidates.recipe: Run: node ../vaultspark-studio-ops/scripts/check-secrets.mjs --for cloudflare.r2. If READY, run: node scripts/ops.mjs blocker-preflight. Then: wrangler r2 bucket create vaultspark-rum, add [[r2_buckets]] binding name="RUM_BUCKET" bucket_name="vaultspark-rum" to wrangler.toml, deploy Worker. Verify by loading the homepage and checking /v/rum receives a beacon POST.

executionLog.note: S162: verified end-to-end — prod deploy 2026-05-25T00:13Z (after S161 binding commit; CF validates r2 bindings at deploy), /v/rum live 202, beacon in ambient bundle. Was completed S161.

candidates.title: Connect check-perf-budget fix recipes to autonomous safe-fix loop
candidates.why: `scripts/check-perf-budget.mjs` already classifies violations and emits `.cache/perf-fix-recipes.json` with ranked concrete fixes (S158). The data structure knows WHAT to fix; only the applier is missing. An autonomous fixer that reads recipes and applies safe-class changes (add `defer` attribute, add `loading=lazy`, inject `<link rel=preload>`, bump resource hints) without human review would close the LCP regression class permanently — not just the current instance.
candidates.recipe: New scripts/auto-apply-perf-fixes.mjs reads .cache/perf-fix-recipes.json, filters to SAFE_AUTO_APPLY class (defer + lazy + preload only — never structural changes), applies fixes idempotently to HTML files, runs build:check, and emits a .cache/perf-fix-applied.json audit trail. Wire into build:check as --auto-fix flag. Run after check-perf-budget when violations exist.

executionLog.note: S162: scripts/auto-apply-perf-fixes.mjs — additive/idempotent/reversible/opt-in/dry-run-default applier (add-resource-hint, add-attr); self-test 6/6; wired --self-test into build:check. No structured actions in current cache by design.

candidates.title: Adaptive /membership/ narrative journey (visit-depth × session-state personalization)
candidates.why: The membership page today presents static tier comparison — the same for a first-time anonymous visitor and a returning logged-in free member. The conversion opportunity is massive: a first-time visitor needs story and intrigue; a returning free member needs a 'what you're missing' delta; a paid member needs to feel the value being delivered. A visit-depth × session-state content switcher (using existing trust-depth.js + intent-state.js signals already wired into the ambient bundle) would turn one flat page into three distinct conversion experiences with zero URL change.
candidates.recipe: In membership/index.html, wrap each content section in data-journey-stage='curious|interested|committed' attributes. In assets/membership-journey.js, read window.VS_TRUST_DEPTH + window.VS_SIGNED_IN + localStorage.vs-visit-count, set body[data-journey-stage], show/hide sections via CSS. Stage 'curious': story + intrigue. Stage 'interested': social proof + live member count. Stage 'committed': what you're missing delta + upgrade CTA with personal stats.

candidates.title: Centralize body[data-vs-signed-in] into assets/signed-in-state.js (single auth query)
candidates.why: S160's account-chip.js, exit-intent.js, and adaptive-cta.js all independently query Supabase for session state — producing 3–4 parallel auth calls on every page load for signed-in users. This is both wasteful (parallel fetches to Supabase add RTT to LCP for authenticated visitors) and brittle (each call site duplicates the error handling + race logic). A single signed-in-state.js that queries once, writes body[data-vs-signed-in], and emits a CustomEvent('vs:session-ready') would consolidate auth overhead and unblock the progressive-membership-journey item.
candidates.recipe: Create assets/signed-in-state.js: on DOMContentLoaded, call VSIdentity.getSession() once, write body[data-vs-signed-in=true|false] + body[data-vs-tier=free|sparked|eternal], dispatch CustomEvent('vs:session-ready', {detail:{session}}). In account-chip.js, exit-intent.js, adaptive-cta.js — replace direct VSIdentity.getSession() calls with addEventListener('vs:session-ready', ...) or body dataset reads. Add to AMBIENT_SOURCES in build-ambient-bundle.mjs as source #1.

candidates.title: Ambient rank progression bar for signed-in members (every page, non-intrusive)
candidates.why: The rank system exists but its progress is only visible when a member explicitly visits /vault-portal/ or /ranks/. An ambient progress indicator — a 2px gradient bar at the very bottom of the viewport (think Duolingo's subtle streak flame, not a banner) showing percentage to next rank — would create persistent micro-motivation without occupying real estate. Members would feel advancement on every page visit, not just when they check their stats. No studio website does this with this level of subtlety.
candidates.recipe: Extend assets/account-chip.js (or signed-in-state.js): after session-ready, fetch /api/member-rank-progress.json (new Supabase RPC endpoint returning {current_points, next_rank_threshold, rank_name}). Inject a <div id=vs-rank-bar> at the bottom of body with CSS: position:fixed; bottom:0; left:0; height:2px; background:var(--vs-gold); width:{pct}%; transition:width 1.2s ease; z-index:1. Animate on first paint. Hide for anonymous users. Store last-known progress in localStorage to prevent flash.

candidates.title: Monthly founder digest: aggregate vault_feedback + micro-feedback into signal surface
candidates.why: The micro-feedback widget and /feedback/ timeline page ship signals but there's no aggregation layer — the founder has to manually read raw rows. A monthly signal digest (new Supabase RPC → `api/feedback-digest.json`, wired to a `/feedback/digest/` page) that buckets feedback by theme (perf, content, nav, bug, compliment), shows sentiment trend, and surfaces the top 3 un-addressed asks would make the feedback loop actually close. Pairs with /ignis/roi/ for a 'we heard → we shipped' narrative.
candidates.recipe: Create scripts/build-feedback-digest.mjs: queries vault_feedback + micro_feedback last 30d, groups by category, counts sentiment, ranks by frequency. Writes api/feedback-digest.json. New /feedback/digest/ page renders bar chart + top asks + last-addressed date. Wire into npm run build. Add link from /feedback/ 'you asked → we shipped' timeline.

executionLog.note: S162: shipped public-safe theme-bucketing on /feedback/insights/ (client-side from existing aggregate views, no raw feedback). Sentiment-trend + top-asks need a server-side categorization cron (backend follow-up, studio-ops-owned).

candidates.title: Live commit-graph as Forge Window studio transparency surface
candidates.why: The Forge Window (/studio-pulse/) shows studio activity but uses synthetic indicators. A live commit graph — built from the GitHub API at build time → committed as api/commit-map.json — would show members the literal DNA of the studio: what shipped, when, which project, commit message. This transparency is a profound trust signal that no comparable studio does. It turns commits into a public artifact of creative labor, not just internal housekeeping. Combined with the IGNIS conduit narration, each commit becomes a legible studio moment.
candidates.recipe: Create scripts/build-commit-map.mjs: calls GitHub API /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits?per_page=50, extracts sha, message, date, author, files changed. Writes api/commit-map.json. On /studio-pulse/, render as a scrollable timeline with project-tag chips. Add commit messages to IGNIS conduit rotation as 'studio made a move' signal type. Wire into npm run build.

executionLog.note: S162: scripts/build-commit-map.mjs (git-log, noise-filtered, self-test 5/5) -> api/commit-map.json; Forge Ledger section + render on /studio-pulse/; wired into build + build:check.

candidates.title: Personalize /oracle/ query suggestions by member rank tier + browsing pattern
candidates.why: The Oracle shows the same query suggestions to a free anonymous visitor and a high-tier Vault member. The signal value diverges massively: a new visitor needs orientation ('what games exist?'); a returning member needs strategy ('what should I focus on to reach Obsidian rank?'). Using the existing session-ready event + tier from signed-in-state.js, the Oracle can swap its suggestion pool dynamically — zero additional API calls, just a different JSON slice served per tier from the existing public-intelligence.js cache.
candidates.recipe: In assets/oracle-interface.js (or wherever Oracle suggestions render), listen for vs:session-ready. On free tier: show exploration queries. On sparked/eternal tier: show strategic rank + challenge queries. On anonymous: show discovery queries. Load query pools from /api/oracle-queries.json (new file, 3 pools, ~1KB). Wire into build via scripts/build-oracle-queries.mjs which reads member rank distribution from IGNIS data.

candidates.title: Upgrade IGNIS conduit from template narration to live IGNIS API sentences
candidates.why: The build-ignis-conduit.mjs script (shipped S160) uses a deterministic verb+subject template to generate IGNIS-voice sentences from git log — cost-neutral and real, but stilted. The studio-ops IGNIS cron infrastructure exists and can call the IGNIS MCP with the last 24h of commits to produce genuinely intelligent narration. The upgrade is a 2-line change in build-ignis-conduit.mjs: replace the template generator with a node scripts/ops.mjs ignis-narrate call when the capability is READY.
candidates.recipe: In scripts/build-ignis-conduit.mjs, after building rawEntries, run: const cap = await resolveCapability('ignis.narrate'); if (cap.ready) { entries = await ignis_narrate(rawEntries); } else { entries = templateNarrate(rawEntries); }. The template narration remains the fallback. No new infrastructure needed — studio-ops already has ignis.narrate as a registered capability.

executionLog.note: S162: capability-gated (resolveCapability ignis.narrate, observability-only per CANON-022/015); respects cron-written narrator=ignis-llm; noise-filtered 7d window; sharpened type-aware acronym-safe template.

candidates.title: Flip nav-sheet default for mobile after founder iPhone verification
candidates.why: nav-sheet.js ships behind ?nav=sheet flag and is fully functional. The founder hasn't yet verified on iPhone. Once verified, flipping shouldActivate() to default-true for (max-width:768px) delivers the modern bottom-sheet nav to all mobile visitors — replacing the drawer that has had 3 regressions (S130, S132, S133). The delta between 'flag-gated proof' and 'default for all' is one boolean change + one DECISIONS.md entry.
candidates.recipe: After founder verifies on iPhone: in assets/nav-sheet.js::shouldActivate(), change the predicate from (hasFlag || hasLocalStorage) to (window.innerWidth <= 768 || hasFlag). Update DECISIONS.md. Remove ?nav=sheet from carry notes. Re-run build:check to confirm no regressions.

executionLog.note: S162: flag readiness confirmed; one-line flip pending founder iPhone verification.

candidates.title: Promote check-perf-budget to --strict mode after LCP fix + 2 clean traces
candidates.why: The perf budget check has been in advisory mode for 3 sessions, waiting for two clean post-deploy samples. Once the LCP regression is fixed (item #1) and two traces confirm < 1.8s on /, this is a one-line change in package.json that promotes the check from warning to build-fail. Every subsequent session gets an automatic regression guard — no more post-hoc trace debugging.
candidates.recipe: After lcp-regression-bisect-fix is complete and two post-push prod traces show / desktop LCP < 1800ms: in package.json build:check, change --check-perf-budget to --check-perf-budget --strict. Run npm run build:check to confirm exit 0.

executionLog.note: S162: dependency unmet — / desktop trace 14528ms > budget would break CI. RUM is the better real-signal gate.

candidates.title: Fix 2 failing compliance doctor probes (30/32 → 32/32)
candidates.why: Doctor shows 11/13 with 2 compliance-related failures. These are structural signals: compliance velocity and compliance validation both failing indicates drift in the canons this project declared. At SIL 988, the marginal point-loss from compliance drift is small, but leaving known failures unaddressed sets a precedent that the gates are advisory. Fix them to preserve the structural integrity of the build.
candidates.recipe: Run: node scripts/ops.mjs doctor --verbose to see the full failure output of the 2 failing probes. Then read the canon they check (likely CANON-006 public-facing branding or CANON-011 sitemap standard) and apply the required changes. Run doctor again to confirm 13/13.

candidates.title: Purge 8 stale ambient shell files (only current hash needed in assets/)
candidates.why: There are 9 `ambient.shell-*.js` files in assets/ but only one is referenced by the current shell. The other 8 are served by GitHub Pages unnecessarily, bloating the deployed surface, confusing `check-orphan-shell-assets`, and adding noise to the asset directory. Each stale file was the canonical bundle at some prior hash — they have no residual value.
candidates.recipe: grep -r 'ambient.shell-' --include='*.html' . | grep src= to find the currently-referenced hash. Delete all ambient.shell-{other}.js files. Run npm run build:check to confirm check-orphan-shell-assets passes clean. Commit as hygiene.

candidates.title: Automate revenue signals freshness (⛔ stale signal in doctor)
candidates.why: Doctor reports revenue signals as stale (⛔). The REVENUE_SIGNALS.md is hand-maintained, which means it only gets updated when someone remembers to update it. Given Stripe webhook data exists in Supabase, a scripts/generate-revenue-signals.mjs that reads Stripe customer count + MRR from Supabase views and writes to portfolio/REVENUE_SIGNALS.md at each build would keep the signal perpetually fresh — turning a manual task into an automated one.
candidates.recipe: Create scripts/generate-revenue-signals.mjs: queries Supabase for vault_members count, sparked_subscribers count, estimated MRR from tier distribution. Writes to portfolio/REVENUE_SIGNALS.md with current date. Wire into npm run build. Doctor probe 'revenue-signals-freshness' should then report ✓ fresh within 24h.

executionLog.note: S162: root cause was a brief-renderer false-negative (sibling REVENUE_SIGNALS.md is fresh; studio-ops auto-generates it). Fixed renderer sibling-fallback so signal flips from BLOCKED to FRESH. Declined literal recipe — committing MRR to a public repo violates the public-safe constraint.
